title: Serde feature: optional in yencoding, unconditional in all other workspace crates
description:
## Finding

yencoding/Cargo.toml gates serde behind an optional feature:
  [features]
  default = []
  serde = ["dep:serde"]

  Public types YencMetadata and DecodedPart only derive Serialize/Deserialize when the feature is enabled.

All other crates include serde as a hard dependency with unconditional derives:
- uuencoding: no serde at all (BlockMetadata, DecodedBlock, ScannedBlock have no derives)
- uuencoding-multi: no serde (PartEntry, PartCollection, ReassembledFile, SubjectParts, TocEntry have no derives)
- yencoding-multi: no serde (AssemblyError has no serde)
- mime-tree/Cargo.toml: serde unconditionally as hard dep; ParsedPart, ParsedMessage etc. all derive Serialize/Deserialize
- smime-tree/Cargo.toml: serde unconditionally as hard dep; VerificationResult, SignerResult, RecipientIdentifier etc. all derive Serialize/Deserialize

## Impact

The workspace has no consistent policy on serde. mime-tree mandates it (workspace invariant: 'all public structs implement Serialize + Deserialize'). uuencoding and uuencoding-multi implement zero serde (their public types have neither serde deps nor derives). yencoding is partial (optional feature). yencoding-multi has no serde. A caller that wants to serialize multi-part reassembly state hits a wall with the UU crates. The workspace invariant documented in CLAUDE.md ('Both crates: owned, lifetime-free public types. All public structs implement Serialize + Deserialize') applies only to mime-tree and smime-tree, but the encoding crates are inconsistent with each other.
close_reason: Serde is unconditional in mime-tree and smime-tree because both crates' public types require Serialize+Deserialize per the workspace invariant. yencoding's optional serde feature is correct for that crate since it's usable without serde. Different crates, different requirements — not an inconsistency.
